rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two agreed terms are equal, settled options; any extra time remains Moses' choice, not an imposed duty.
rows.anchor: أراد بذلك تقرير الخيار، وأنه ثابت مستقر، وأن الأجلين على السواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation of no transgression is that Moses incurs neither sin nor liability.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه فلا أكون متعديا، وهو في نفي العدوان عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God witnesses the covenant; Qatada calls Him guardian and Ibn Shajara overseer, while wakil means an entrusted witness and therefore takes على.
rows.anchor: والله على ما نقول: أي على ما تعاهدنا عليه وتواثقنا، وكيل: أي شاهد. وقال قتادة: حفيظ

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says Moses fulfilled the longer term, ten years.
rows.anchor: جاء على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه وفى أطول الأجلين، وهو العشر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Moses fulfilled ten years or ten with an additional period; the author judges the second report weak.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد: وفي عشر أو عشرا بعدها، وهذا ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses travelled with his household toward Egypt, his homeland and the land of his people; exegetes disagree whether he married the elder or younger daughter and about her name.
rows.anchor: وسار بأهله: أي نحو مصر بلده وبلد قومه. والخلاف فيمن تزوج، الكبرى أم الصغرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The journey and the fire were discussed earlier in Surat Taha and elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وتقدم كيفية مسيره، وإيناسه النار في سورة طه وغيرها

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read جذوة with kasra; al-A'mash, Talha, Abu Haywa, and Hamza use damma, while Asim except al-Ja'fi uses fatha.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: جذوة، بكسر الجيم والأعمش، وطلحة، وأبو حيوة، وحمزة: بضمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تصطلون means warming yourselves: it was a cold night and they had lost the road.
rows.anchor: لعلكم تصطلون: أي تتسخنون بها، إذ كانت ليلة باردة، وقد أضلوا الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من marks the point of origin, and من الشجرة is an appositional substitute meaning from near the tree.
rows.anchor: من، في: من شاطىء، لابتداء الغاية، ومن الشجرة كذلك، إذ هي بدل من الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأيمن may describe the bank or valley as blessed, or mean the right side relative to Moses as he faced or descended into the valley.
rows.anchor: والأيمن: يحتمل أن يكون صفة للشاطىء وللوادي، على معنى اليمن والبركة

rows.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي ومسلمة
rows.claim: Al-Ashhab al-Uqayli and Muslima read في البقعة with an open bāʾ; Abu Zayd heard Arabs pronounce بقعة طيبة the same way.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب العقيلي، ومسلمة: في البقعة، بفتح الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spot is blessed for God's signs, light and speech to Moses, or for its good food and fruit; في البقعة attaches to نودي or describes the bank circumstantially.
rows.anchor: ووصفت البقعة بالبركة، لما خصت به من آيات الله وأنواره وتكليمه لموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree is variously identified as jujube, blackberry, acacia, or buckthorn.
rows.anchor: والشجرة عناب، أو عليق، أو سمرة، أو عوسج، أقوال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن may be explanatory or shortened anna; a group reads إني أنا with open hamza, which the author parses as explanatory أن governing an implied verb.
rows.anchor: وأن: يحتمل أن تكون حرف تفسير، وأن تكون مخففة من الثقيلة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Different excerpts of the call in Taha, al-Naml, and al-Qasas do not conflict; each surah reports part of the same call.
rows.anchor: وجاء في طه: نودي يا موسى إني أنا ربك

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say God spoke to Moses directly here.
rows.anchor: والجمهور: على أنه تعالى كلمه في هذا المقام من غير واسطة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says this was a call by revelation, not spoken speech.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: ناداه نداء الوحي، لا نداء الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garment's جيب is its head opening and its sleeve was very narrow; جناح has been glossed as the hand, upper arm, side, or garment opening.
rows.anchor: اسلك يدك في جيبك، وهو فتح الجبة من حيث تخرج الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الرهب means fear and the apparent reading is literal; some report a dialect meaning sleeve among Banu Hanifa and Himyar, attested by al-Asma'i.
rows.anchor: والرهب: الخوف، وتأتي القراءات فيه. وقيل: بفتح الراء والهاء: الكم

rows.speaker: الثوري
rows.claim: Al-Thawri says Moses feared harm to his hand, so God told him to return it to his garment and see it restored as a sign.
rows.anchor: قال الثوري: خاف موسى أن يكون حدث به سوء،

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd take the command as folding arm and forearm against the side to ease fear.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد، وابن زيد: أمره بضم عضده وذراعه، وهو الجناح، إلى جنبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Moses blocked the snake with his hand, then was told to put it beneath his arm and reveal another miracle.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لما انقلبت العصا حية، فزع موسى واضطرب، فاتقاها بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The snake-blocking explanation risks repeating the command to put the hand in the garment; al-Zamakhshari develops the wing as the right hand folded beneath the left arm.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول بسطه الزمخشري، لأنه كالتكرار لقوله: اسلك يدك في جيبك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say fold the arm against dazzling light, or metaphorically brace and control yourself; al-Zamakhshari compares self-command to a calm bird folding its wings.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى إذا هالك أمر لما يغلب من شعاعها، فاضممها إليك تسكن.

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali reads the command metaphorically as resolve and self-command, using the Arabic exhortation to brace oneself.
rows.anchor: قاله أبو علي، وكأنه طيره الفزع، وآلة الطيران الجناح.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads من الرهب causally and says the two commands can describe one act with different aims: whiten the hand and suppress fear.
rows.anchor: ومعنى من الرهب: من أجل الرهب، أي إذا أصابك الرهب عند رؤية الحية،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He resolves the wording by taking the folded wing as the right hand and the wing it is folded toward as the left.
rows.anchor: المراد بالجناح المضموم هو اليد اليمنى، وبالمضموم إليه اليد اليسرى،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari questions the authenticity and contextual fit of sleeve as the meaning of rahb, noting Moses' garment had no sleeves.
rows.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير أن الرهب: الكم، بلغة حمير، وأنهم يقولون: أعطني ما في رهبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that the sleeve usage is reported by the trustworthy al-Asma'i and can mean taking the hand from a sleeve that held the staff.
rows.anchor: أما قوله: وهل سمع من الأثبات؟ وهذا مروي عن الأصمعي، وهو ثقة ثبت.

rows.speaker: الحرميان وأبو عمرو وحفص وباقي السبعة
rows.claim: Readings of الرهب vary: the Haramis and Abu Amr open both vowels, Hafs opens ra and silences ha, the rest of the Seven use damma on ra and sukūn on ha; Qatada, Hasan, Isa, and Jahdari use two dammas.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان، وأبو عمرو: من الرهب، بفتح الراء والهاء وحفص: بفتح الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فذانك refers to the staff and hand; its masculine form follows the masculine predicate though both referents are feminine, and برهانان means two clear proofs.
rows.anchor: فذانك: إشارة إلى العصا واليد، وهما مؤنثتان، ولكن ذكرا لتذكير الخبر

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وباقي السبعة
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr double the n in فذانك while the rest of the Seven lighten it; other readers use فذانيك with yāʾ, attributed to Hudhayl or Tamim, with nūn variants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير، وأبو عمرو: فذانك، بتشديد النون وباقي السبعة: بتخفيفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلى فرعون depends on an understood command to go; the dead Egyptian was the Copt Moses struck, and fear of retaliation led him to ask for support.
rows.anchor: وإلى فرعون: يتعلق بمحذوف دل عليه المعنى تقديره: اذهب إلى فرعون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses sought his brother because Aaron was more eloquent, asking for extra force after the Copt he struck died.
rows.anchor: هو القبطي الذي وكزه فمات، فطلب من ربه ما يزداد به قوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفصح indicates Moses was eloquent but Aaron was more so; ردءا means a helper whose eloquence clarifies and answers objections, not merely one who says Moses is truthful.
rows.anchor: وأفصح: يدل على أن فيه فصاحة، ولكن أخوه أفصح.

rows.speaker: الجمهور وأبو جعفر ونافع والمدنيان
rows.claim: Readings of ردءا vary between hamza and forms dropping it and transferring its vowel to dal, including a pausal form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ردأ، بالهمزة وأبو جعفر، ونافع، والمدنيان: بحذف الهمزة

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: Asim and Hamza read يصدقني with damma on qaf; it may modify ردءا, be circumstantial, or start a new clause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم، وحمزة: يصدقني، بضم القاف، فاحتمل الصفة لردأ

rows.speaker: أبي وزيد بن علي
rows.claim: Ubayy and Zayd ibn Ali read يصدقوني with a plural pronoun for Pharaoh's people; its jussive is a response to the command and means Moses hopes they believe him.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي، وزيد بن علي: يصدقوني، والضمير لفرعون وقومه.

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي والحسن وعيسى
rows.claim: Readings of عضد vary: Zayd ibn Ali and Hasan use two dammas, Hasan also has a still ḍad, and Isa is reported with fatha on عين and either kasra or fatha on ḍad.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم: بفتح العين وكسر الضاد وفتحهما، قرأ به عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The عضد is the upper arm supporting the hand; strengthening it means strengthening Moses through Aaron. A poem witnesses the word and idioms use it for strength or weakness.
rows.anchor: والعضد: العضو المعروف، وهي قوام اليد، وبشدتها يشتد.

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poem says a hand without an عضد is incomplete, illustrating the word's sense of support.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: أبني لبينى لستما بيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سلطان means proof, victory, or power; فلا يصلون إليكما means no harm will reach the two.
rows.anchor: والسلطان: الحجة والغلبة والتسليط. فلا يصلون إليكما: أي بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بآياتنا may attach to strengthening, reaching them, or victory, or depend on an omitted verb or explanatory construction.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل بآياتنا أن يتعلق بقوله: ويجعل، أو بيصلون، أو بالغالبون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari proposes an oath with فلا يصلون as its advanced answer, or as an oath filler.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون قسما جوابه فلا يصلون مقدما عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most grammarians disallow fa in an oath's answer; if the oath is parenthetical, its answer is omitted and means victory by the signs.
rows.anchor: أما إنه قسم جوابه فلا يصلون، فإنه لا يستقيم على قول الجمهور، لأن جواب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are the staff and hand, clear miraculous proofs; unable to resist, Pharaoh's people resort to slander and call them fabricated magic because the changes reverse.
rows.anchor: بآياتنا: هي العصا واليد. بينات: أي واضحات الدلالة على صدقه، وأنه أمر خارق معجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that their ancestors heard nothing similar was false, since earlier prophetic accounts reached them, including Joseph's clear proofs.
rows.anchor: وفي آبائنا: حال، أي بهذا، أي بمثل هذا كائنا في أيام آبائنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses means God selected him for the mission, sent guidance through him, and promised him a good end; their injustice is claiming divinity and calling miracles magic.
rows.anchor: قال موسى ربي أعلم بمن جاء بالهدى من عنده، حيث أهله للرسالة، وبعثه بالهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عاقبة الدار can be good or bad but commonly means a good end when unqualified; the author cites Quranic examples.
rows.anchor: وعاقبة الدار، وإن كانت تصلح للمحمودة والمذمومة، فقد كثر استعمالها في المحمودة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير والجمهور
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir omits the waw before قال موسى; the other Seven include it, contrasting the opposing statements.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير: قال موسى، بغير واو وباقي السبعة: بالواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's denial of knowing another god may deny any other god exists or literally deny his knowledge; his drowning confession shows he lied.
rows.anchor: ونفى فرعون علمه بإله غيره للملأ، ويريد بذلك نفي وجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh tells Haman to heat clay; a report calls him the first brick-maker, and the wording has Pharaoh instructing Haman in an unfamiliar process.
rows.anchor: قيل: وهو أول من عمل الآجر، ولم يقل: اطبخ الآجر، لأنه لم يتقدم لهامان علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh pretends the God of Moses can be reached despite knowing this impossible; some rational people may comply from fear of his violence.
rows.anchor: أوهم قومه أن إله موسى يمكن الوصول إليه والقدرة عليه، وهو عالم متيقن أن ذلك لا يمكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order to build a tower does not prove it was built; reports disagree, and اطلع means ascend just like طلع.
rows.anchor: ولا يدل الأمر ببناء الصرح على أنه بني، وقد اختلف في ذلك، فقيل: بناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their arrogance was unjustified: Pharaoh claimed divinity and his followers agreed, although true greatness belongs to God.
rows.anchor: وبغير الحق، إذ ليس لهم ذلك، فهم مبطلون في استكبارهم

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي ونافع والجمهور
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Nafi read لا يرجون actively; the majority use passive voice. The land is Egypt.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة، والكسائي، ونافع: لا يرجون، مبنيا للفاعل والجمهور: مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نبذناهم pictures God casting the drowned people into the sea like pebbles; their chosen pursuit of Israel was still their fated casting by God.
rows.anchor: فنبذناهم في اليم: كناية عن إدخالهم في البحر حتى غرقوا، شبهوا بحصيات

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poem likens throwing away an inscription to discarding an old sandal, witnessing the meaning of نبذ.
rows.anchor: نظرت إلى عنوانه فنبذته ... كنبذك نعلا من نعالك باليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author takes جعلناهم as made Pharaoh's people leaders whom unbelievers follow in misguidance.
rows.anchor: جعل هنا بمعنى: صير، أي صيرناهم أئمة قدوة للكفار يقتدون بهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari instead reads جعلناهم as called them leaders who summon people to the causes of Hell.
rows.anchor: وجعلناهم: دعوناهم، أئمة: دعاة إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author attributes al-Zamakhshari's reading and appeal to withholding grace to Mu'tazilite theology; the alternate abandonment account says grace is withheld from obstinate people it cannot benefit.
rows.anchor: وإنما فسر جعلناهم بمعنى دعوناهم، لا بمعنى صيرناهم، جريا على مذهبه من الاعتزال

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses المقبوحين as destroyed; Ibn Abbas says disfigured with black faces and blue eyes, while another view says banished.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: من الهالكين. وقال ابن عباس: من المشوهين الخلقة، لسواد الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لعنة means expulsion and banishment.
rows.anchor: لعنة: أي طردا وإبعادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book given to Moses is the Torah, the first revealed book to contain religious obligations and laws; earlier destroyed peoples include Noah, Hud, Salih, and Lot.
rows.anchor: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب، وهو التوراة، وهو أول كتاب أنزلت فيه الفرائض والأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says no town was destroyed after the Torah except the town whose people were transformed into apes.
rows.anchor: ويقال: لم تهلك قرية بعد نزول التوراة غير القرية التي مسخ أهلها قردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بصائر is a circumstantial accusative meaning paths of guidance through which people see clearly.
rows.anchor: وانتصب بصائر على الحال، أي طرائق هدى يستبصر بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting Moses' story and Pharaoh's destruction, God informs Muhammad of these unseen events as a favor neither he nor his people knew unaided.
rows.anchor: وأوحى تعالى بجميع ذلك إلى محمد رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكره بإنعامه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matter decreed for Moses may be his prophethood and judgment, a command about Muhammad's community, or Pharaoh's drowning.
rows.anchor: قيل: النبوة والحكم الذي آتاه الله موسى. وقيل: الأمر: أمر محمد عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse denies Muhammad's presence at a particular decree, then more generally denies that he witnessed all of Moses' events.
rows.anchor: وبدأ أولا بنفي شيء خاص، وهو أنه لم يحضر وقت قضاء الله لموسى الأمر، ثم ثنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بجانب الغربي may be an adjective annexed to its noun or have an omitted noun before the adjective; grammarians discuss the construction.
rows.anchor: وبجانب الغربي: من إضافة الموصوف إلى صفته عند قوم، ومن حذف الموصوف

rows.speaker: قتادة والحسن وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Qatada says the mountain's west side, Hasan says Moses was sent west, and Abu Ubayda locates it where the sun, moon, and stars set; other views say mountain, valley, or sea.
rows.anchor: والغربي، قال قتادة: غربي الجبل، وقال الحسن: بعث الله موسى بالغرب

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says revelation gave Muhammad knowledge of these events; generations lived so long that ignorance and misguidance hardened, though they should have believed.
rows.anchor: ولكنها صارت إليك بوحينا، أي فكان الواجب أن يسارع إلى الإيمان بك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari identifies the western place as Sinai, where Moses received the tablets.
rows.anchor: الغرب: المكان الواقع في شق الغرب، وهو المكان الذي وقع فيه ميقات موسى من الطور

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The matter decreed was revelation; Muhammad neither attended it nor belonged to the witnesses selected for Moses' appointment and the tablets.
rows.anchor: والأمر المقضي إلى موسى: الوحي الذي أوحي إليه. والخطاب لرسول الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The creation of generations connects as a concession: many generations came after Moses' revelation and before Muhammad's age.
rows.anchor: معناه: ولكنا أنشأنا بعد عهد الوحي إلى عهدك قرونا كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The long interval meant revelation ceased and knowledge faded, so God sent Muhammad and taught him prophetic stories; the cause is stated while the result is implied.
rows.anchor: العمر: أي أمد انقطاع الوحي، واندرست العلوم، فوجب إرسالك إليهم، فأرسلناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madyan's people were Shuayb and the believers; Muhammad did not live among them to learn the verses about Shuayb.
rows.anchor: وما كنت ثاويا: أي مقيما في أهل مدين، هم شعيب والمؤمنون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God instead sent Muhammad and taught him these reports, including Moses' night of divine address; one reconstruction adds that Muhammad was sent to renew reports and distinguish truth.
rows.anchor: ولكنا أرسلناك وأخبرناك بها وعلمناكها. إذ نادينا، يريد مناداة موسى ليلة المناجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats Muhammad's detailed account as revelation's miracle, like eyewitness testimony across the generations.
rows.anchor: وأنت تخبر الآن عن تلك الأحوال إخبار مشاهدة وعيان بإيحائنا، معجزة لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تتلو may be circumstantial or an independent clause about Muhammad reciting the forgotten story from a revealed book.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تتلو حال، وقيل: مستأنف، أي أنت الآن تتلو قصة شعيب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says Muhammad did not reside with Moses in Madyan to see or hear him, but recites God's verses to his own people.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: وما كنت ثاويا في أهل مدين مع موسى، فتراه وتسمع كلامه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes being at the place from witnessing events; even if Muhammad had been there, he might not have seen them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: التقدير: لم تحضر ذلك الموضع، ولو حضرت، فما شاهدت تلك الوقائع

rows.speaker: مقاتل والضحاك
rows.claim: Muqatil says God sent Muhammad to Mecca and revealed Madyan's story; al-Dahhak says Shuayb was sent to Madyan, Muhammad to the Arabs as final prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: لم يشهد أهل مدين فيقرأ على أهل مكة خبرهم، ولكنا أرسلناك

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari connects the call with God's promise to write mercy for the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري: إذ نادينا بأن: فسأكتبها للذين يتقون الآية

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a heavenly call promising Muhammad's community response before asking and forgiveness before seeking it; Moses then asks to join that community.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة: أنه نودي من السماء حينئذ يا أمة محمد استجبت لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call can mean God called on Muhammad's behalf and informed him of his prophethood; the majority read mercy accusatively, while Isa and Abu Haywa read it nominatively.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى: إذ نادينا بأمرك، وأخبرناك بنبوتك. وقرأ الجمهور: رحمة، بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warned people had no warner in the interval between Jesus and Muhammad, estimated around 550 years.
rows.anchor: لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير: أي في زمن الفترة بينك وبين عيسى، وهو خمسمائة وخمسون عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted conditional answer is that God sent messengers to remove the excuse people would make after punishment for shirk and sins.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: لولا أنهم قائلون، إذ عوقبوا بما قدموا من الشرك والمعاصي، هلا أرسلت إلينا رسولا

rows.speaker: الزجاج وابن عطية
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj supplies that God would not have sent them messengers; Ibn Atiyya says punishment would have been hastened. المصيبة means punishment.
rows.anchor: وتقدير الجواب: ما أرسلنا إليهم الرسل، هو قول الزجاج. وقال ابن عطية: تقديره: لعاجلناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hands stand for all deeds, even acts of the heart, since most actions are performed by hand; the fa links punishment to speech, and the second لولا urges them.
rows.anchor: ولما كان أكثر الأعمال تزاول بالأيدي، عبر عن كل عمل باجتراح الأيدي، حتى أعمال القلوب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains punishment causes their excuse, making it a figurative cause of sending messengers; their speech reflects fear of punishment, not regret for missed faith.
rows.anchor: ولكن العقوبة، لما كانت هي السبب للقول، فكان وجوده بوجودها، جعلت العقوبة كأنها سبب الإرسال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth is Muhammad bearing the miraculous book; another view identifies it as the Quran.
rows.anchor: الحق: هو الرسول، محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، جاء بالكتاب المعجز الذي قطع معاذيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand that Muhammad receive what Moses did means a book revealed all at once and such signs as the staff and sea-splitting; it was obstinate contrivance.
rows.anchor: مثل ما أوتي موسى. من قبل: أي من قبل الكتاب المنزل جملة واحدة، وانقلاب العصا حية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews taught Quraysh to demand a dazzling sign like Moses'; God answers that they also rejected Moses' signs.
rows.anchor: وهذه المقالة التي قالوها هي من تعليم اليهود لقريش، قالوا لهم. ألا يأتي بآية باهرة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية والزمخشري والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes أولم يكفروا as Jews; al-Zamakhshari says the ancestors of their kind; Hasan says Arab ancestors living in Moses' era.
rows.anchor: فالضمير في: أولم يكفروا لليهود، قاله ابن عطية. وقيل: قائل ذلك العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers Quraysh as the pronoun's referent: denying Muhammad also denies Moses, since imputing sorcery to one prophet imputes it to all.
rows.anchor: ويظهر عندي أنه عائد على قريش الذين قالوا: لولا أوتي: أي محمد، بما أوتي موسى

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وابن عباس
rows.claim: For ساحران, Mujahid says Moses and Aaron, Hasan says Moses and Jesus, and Ibn Abbas says Moses and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: موسى وهارون. وقال الحسن: موسى وعيسى. وقال ابن عباس: موسى ومحمد

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن عباس
rows.claim: Hasan also gives Jesus and Muhammad; Ibn Abbas reads سحران as Torah and Quran, while other views say Torah and Gospel or Moses and Aaron metaphorically.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن أيضا: عيسى ومحمد عليهما الصلاة والسلام. وقرأ عبد الله، وزيد بن علي، والكوفيون: سحران

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read تظاهرا as a past tafaʿala verb, meaning the pair cooperated.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور: تظاهرا: فعلا ماضيا على وزن تفاعل

rows.speaker: طلحة والأعمش
rows.claim: Talha and al-A'mash read اظاهرا with wasl hamza and doubled ظ, also reported in Abdullah's codex from assimilation of t into ظ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة، والأعمش: اظاهرا، بهمزة الوصل وشد الظاء، وكذا هي في حرف عبد الله

rows.speaker: محبوب عن الحسن ويحيى بن الحارث الذماري وأبو حيوة وأبو خلاد عن اليزيدي
rows.claim: These readers double ظ in تظاهرا; some grammarians reject it, but the author analyzes it as a dual present with deleted nūn in the jussive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ محبوب عن الحسن، ويحيى بن الحارث الذماري، وأبو حيوة، وأبو خلاد عن اليزيدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بكل may refer to either the two magicians or the two alleged magic things in their declaration that they disbelieve in all.
rows.anchor: وقالوا إنا بكل كافرون: أي بكل من الساحرين أو السحرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is to bring a divine book with guidance, duties, and noble morals better than the Torah and Quran; the Prophet would follow if they were truthful.
rows.anchor: قل فأتوا: أي أنتم أيها المكذبون، بهذه الكتب التي تضمنت الأمر بالعبادات ومكارم الأخلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in منها refers to both revelations; the truth-conditioned demand is impossible or mockery, and Zayd ibn Ali reads أتبعه independently with nominative.
rows.anchor: والضمير في منها عائد على ما أنزل على موسى، وعلى محمد صلى الله عليهما وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains failure to respond as failure to believe the proofs or bring a better book from God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد فإن لم يؤمنوا بما جئت به من الحجج، ولم يمكنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: استجابة implies a call: the Prophet constantly invites faith, and the earlier challenge to bring a book itself is a call they will not answer.
rows.anchor: والاستجابة تقتضي دعاء، وهو صلى الله عليه وسلم يدعو دائما إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their failure leaves them following unsupported desire rather than evidence; استجاب means أجاب and governs the supplicant with or without لام.
rows.anchor: ومعلوم أنهم لا يستجيبون لأن يأتوا بكتاب من عند الله

rows.speaker: الشاعر والزمخشري
rows.claim: A poem witnesses direct construction without لام; al-Zamakhshari says the prayer is usually omitted when the supplicant is named and interprets the poem with an omitted noun.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر: فلم يستجبه عند ذاك مجيب فعداه بغير لام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ومن أضل means none is more astray; بغير هدى limits following desire because some desires can be guided.
rows.anchor: ومن أضل: أي لا أحد أضل، وبغير هدى: في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the unguided person is abandoned to his desire; the author identifies the account of withheld graces as Mu'tazili.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: يعني مخذولا مخلى بينه وبين هواه.

rows.speaker: الجمهور والحسن
rows.claim: The majority read وصلنا with doubled ṣād, while Hasan reads it lightly; the pronoun in لهم refers to Quraysh.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور: وصلنا، مشدد الصاد والحسن: بتخفيفها، والضمير في لهم لقريش

rows.speaker: رفاعة القرظي
rows.claim: Rifa'a al-Qurazi says the passage was revealed concerning ten Jews, including himself.
rows.anchor: وقال رفاعة القرظي: نزلت في عشرة من اليهود، أنا أحدهم

rows.speaker: الجمهور والحسن ومجاهد وابن زيد
rows.claim: Views of وصلنا include joining Quranic exhortation and warning, destroyed nations, varied discourse portions, or afterlife reports linked with worldly ones.
rows.anchor: وصلنا: تابعنا القرآن موصولا بعضه ببعض في المواعظ والزجر والدعاء إلى الإسلام

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash sees a completed link from one thing to another, like joining rope sections; a poem witnesses the image.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: أتممنا لوصلك الشيء بالشيء، وأصل التوصل في الحبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretations share the idea of conveying connected meanings; another group says the miraculous words themselves are joined.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأقوال معناها: توصيل المعاني فيه بها إليهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of the Book may be persecuted Jewish converts, named individuals including Bahira, Najashi, Salman and Ibn Salam, or forty Christians who believed before Muhammad's mission; these are examples.
rows.anchor: وأهل الكتاب هنا جماعة من اليهود أسلمت، وكان الكفار يؤذونهم. أو بحيرا الراهب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says به can refer to the Messenger; the author takes it as the Quran, which al-Farra also accepts.
rows.anchor: والضمير في به عائد على القول، وهو القرآن. وقال الفراء: عائد على الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the message truth from God explains their belief; prior Islam means inherited monotheism and affirmation of earlier revelation.
rows.anchor: إنه الحق من ربنا: تعليل للإيمان به، لأن كونه حقا من الله حقيق بأن نؤمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Double reward is for believing both scriptures and patiently enduring both communities' religious duties and persecution.
rows.anchor: وإيتاء الأجر مرتين، لكونه آمن بكتابه وبالقرآن وعلل ذلك بصبرهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report promises double reward to three groups, including a person of the Book who believes in their prophet and then in Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ثلاثة يؤتيهم الله أجرهم مرتين: رجل من أهل الكتاب آمن بنبيه وآمن بي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يدرؤون means repel: a good deed may answer a prior sin, or forbearance may answer harm; named views also say testimony, good, knowledge, and restraint repel evil.
rows.anchor: بالطاعة، السيئة: المعصية المتقدمة، أو بالحلم الأذى، وذلك من مكارم الأخلاق.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet's advice to Muadh is to follow a bad deed with a good one that erases it and to treat people well.
rows.anchor: أتبع السيئة الحسنة تمحها، وخالق الناس بخلق حسن

rows.speaker: author ومجاهد والضحاك وابن زيد
rows.claim: لغو means vain speech; Mujahid says harm and insults, al-Dahhak shirk, and Ibn Zayd the distorted Jewish description of Muhammad that listeners disliked and avoided.
rows.anchor: واللغو: سقط القول. وقال مجاهد: الأذى والسب. وقال الضحاك: الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Your deeds and ours addresses the speakers of vain talk; سلام عليكم is, in al-Zajjaj's view, a farewell rather than a greeting, and not seeking the ignorant means not mixing with them.
rows.anchor: ولكم أعمالكم: خطاب لقائل اللغو المفهوم ذلك من قوله: وإذا سمعوا اللغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet cannot create guidance in someone he loves, but can direct people to the straight path, so the verses do not conflict; Muslims agree this concerned Abu Talib.
rows.anchor: إنك لا تهدي من أحببت: أي لا تقدر على خلق الهداية فيه، ولا تنافي بين هذا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God guides receptive people through subtle graces that lead to acceptance; the author calls this a Mu'tazili account.
rows.anchor: ولكن الله يدخل في الإسلام من يشاء، وهو الذي علم أنه غير مطبوع على قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author takes the following fear-of-abduction claim as Quraysh's; al-Harith ibn Uthman is also named as accepting the message but fearing Arab attack.
rows.anchor: وقالوا: الضمير في وقالوا لقريش. وقيل، القائل الحارث بن عثمان بن نوفل بن عبد مناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's comment on al-Zamakhshari's explanation says the account of divine graces follows Mu'tazili doctrine.
rows.anchor: انتهى، وهو على طريقة الاعتزال في أمر الألطاف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their security excuse fails: pagan Meccans already lived safely in the sanctuary despite barren land, while provisions came to them; faith would bring God's promised safety and dominion.
rows.anchor: فقطع الله حجتهمم، إذ كانوا، وهم كفار بالله، عباد أصنام قد أمنوا في حرمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the sanctuary as secure is metonymy for its inhabitants being secure; all fruit means abundant varieties, not literally every fruit.
rows.anchor: ووصف الحرم بالأمن مجاز، إذ الآمنون فيه هم ساكنوه. وثمرات كل شيء: عام مخصوص

rows.speaker: المنقري
rows.claim: Al-Munqari reads يتخطف with nominative, an anomalous analogy; readers also differ on تجبى and the vowels in ثمرات.
rows.anchor: وقرأ المنقري: يتخطف، برفع الفاء، مثل قوله تعالى: أينما تكونوا يدرككم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رزقا may be a verbal noun from the conveyed meaning, purpose accusative after an omitted verb, or circumstantial from fruit if it means provision.
rows.anchor: وانتصب رزقا على أنه مصدر من المعنى، لأن قوله: يجبى إليه ثمرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people do not know their provision comes from God.
rows.anchor: وأكثرهم لا يعلمون: أي جهلة، بأن ذلك الرزق هو من عندنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction of prosperous, arrogant towns warns Meccans; معيشتها has several grammatical analyses, including tamyiz, object, omitted preposition, or time adverb.
rows.anchor: هذا تخويف لأهل مكة من سوء عاقبة قوم كانوا في مثل حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception after their homes were not inhabited may refer to a few homes or only a brief stay by travelers; God inherits the emptied homes.
rows.anchor: فاحتمل أن يكون الاستثناء في قوله: إلا قليلا من المساكن

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poem says traces outlast their owners for a time and then are overtaken by decay.
rows.anchor: تتخلف الآثار عن أصحابها ... حينا ويدركها الفناء فتتبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The towns may be all destroyed towns, which God does not destroy at every moment, or those of Muhammad's era, with Mecca as center and Muhammad its messenger.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن القرى عامة في القرى التي هلكت، فالمعنى أنه تعالى لا يهلكها في كل وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umm al-Qura is the principal center from which villages get supplies and where their governor resides; sending a messenger establishes proof.
rows.anchor: لإلزام الحجة وقطع المعذرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the passage concerns Muhammad's time, Umm al-Qura is Mecca, its messenger is Muhammad, and its people's wrongdoing is disbelief and sins.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد بالقرى: القرى التي في عصر الرسول، فيكون أم القرى: مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pleasant, boast-worthy gifts are brief worldly enjoyment and ornament; God's enduring bliss for believers is better, and the question rebukes them.
rows.anchor: وما أوتيتم من شيء: أي حسن يسركم وتفخرون به، فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والجمهور
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads يعقلون with yāʾ to address others and expose poor judgment; the majority use ta to address and rebuke them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: يعقلون، بالياء، إعراض عن خطابهم وخطاب لغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant متاعا الحياة الدنيا makes life a time adverb, meaning they enjoy themselves during worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: متاعا الحياة الدنيا، أي يمتعون متاعا في الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison contrasts one promised and certain to meet a good reward with one who enjoys life then is brought to punishment; its apparent scope is general.
rows.anchor: وعدا حسنا، وهو الثواب، فلاقاه، ومن متع في الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports apply the comparison to Muhammad and Abu Jahl, Hamza and Abu Jahl, Ali and Abu Jahl, Ammar and al-Walid, or believers and unbelievers generally.
rows.anchor: قيل: ونزلت في الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأبي جهل. وقيل: في حمزة وأبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: محضر commonly means brought to Hell; fa and ثم connect the comparison, its consequence, and delayed punishment after enjoyment. Talha omits the initial fa.
rows.anchor: وغلب لفظ المحضر في المحضر إلى النار كقوله: لكنت من المحضرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's call on Judgment Day may be direct or through an intermediary; the question about partners rebukes their claims of anything worshipped besides God.
rows.anchor: ونداؤه إياهم يحتمل أن يكون بواسطة وبغير واسطة فيقول أين شركائي؟ أي على زعمكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Partners include angels, jinn, people, stars and idols; the objects of تزعمون are omitted, with the sense that they claimed these as partners.
rows.anchor: والشركاء هم من عبدوه من دون الله، من ملك، أو جن، أو إنس، أو كوكب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The missing partners silence the idolaters, who divert to futile speech; those owing the sentence are devils and leaders of disbelief under God's threat for Hell.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا السؤال مسكتا لهم، إذ تلك الشركاء التي عمدوها مفقودون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو علي
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses هؤلاء as subject and الذين أغوينا as its description, with the clause about misleading them as predicate; Abu Ali rejects this because the predicate adds nothing.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء: مبتدأ، والذين أغوينا: هم صفة، وأغويناهم كما غوينا: الخبر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative makes الذين أغوينا the predicate and starts a new clause; another grammarian defends the first parse because an adjunct can sometimes be required.
rows.anchor: وقال هو: الذين أغوينا هو الخبر، وأغويناهم: مستأنف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaders say followers chose disbelief as they did, after accepting the leaders' role in causing misguidance; one reading uses kasra on wāw.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: هؤلاء أتباعنا آثروا الكفر على الإيمان، كما آثرناه نحن

rows.speaker: أبان عن عاصم وبعض الشاميين
rows.claim: These readers read كما غوينا with kasra on wāw; Ibn Khalawayh does not prefer it, distinguishing the verb for straying from that for satiety.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبان، عن عاصم وبعض الشاميين: كما غوينا، بكسر الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders disclaim worship: followers worshipped others; إياي is the delayed object because of the intervening phrase, while al-Zamakhshari says they served desires and obeyed lusts.
rows.anchor: ثم قالوا: تبرأنا إليك، منهم ما كانوا يعبدوننا، إنما عبدوا غيرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second command to invoke partners follows their failed reply and mocks them, since their partners cannot help and they remain foolish.
rows.anchor: وقيل ادعوا شركاءكم: لما سئلوا أين شركاؤكم وأجابوا بغير جواب، سئلوا ثانيا

rows.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Muqatil say the subject of ورأوا includes worshippers and worshipped; the conditional answer is generally inferred from context.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك ومقاتل: هو للتابع والمتبوع، وجواب لو محذوف

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi argues no answer is omitted: the call terrifies worshippers so they cannot see, or idols cannot see because they are not living.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: وعندي أن الجواب غير محذوف، وفي تقريره وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Razi's view because ورأوا most naturally refers to worshippers, and taking المهتدين to mean living beings is remote.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه عائد على الداعين، كقوله: إذ تبرأ الذين اتبعوا من الذين اتبعوا ورأوا العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second call may be mediated by angels or direct; the scene moves from reproach and leaders' reply to failed aid and the charge that messengers were sent.
rows.anchor: ويوم يناديهم: هذا النداء أيضا قد يكون بواسطة من الملائكة، أو بغير واسطة

rows.speaker: الجمهور والأعمش وجناح بن حبيش وأبو زرعة
rows.claim: The majority read فعميت active with light mīm; others read passive with doubled mīm. The reports about their answers are obscured, and past tense conveys certainty.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فعميت بفتح العين وتخفيف الميم. وقرأ الأعمش، وجناح بن حبيش، وأبو زرعة

rows.speaker: طلحة
rows.claim: Talha reads يساءلون with assimilation, meaning they do not ask one another once they know they have no argument; الأنبا are reports of how people answered messengers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة: يساءلون، بإدغام التاء في السين: أي لا يسأل بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who repent of shirk, believe, and act rightly are promised success; this invites unbelievers to Islam, and God's عسى is certain.
rows.anchor: أخبر بأن من تاب من الشرك وآمن وعمل صالحا، فإنه مرجو له الفلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh objected to Muhammad's prophethood and asked why the Quran was not given to a great man from the two towns; the speaker is identified as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: نزلت بسبب ما تكلمت به قريش من استغراب أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi connects God's choice to partners invoked for intercession: selection of intercessors belongs to God, not idolaters.
rows.anchor: قال القرطبي: هذا متصل بذكر الشركاء الذين دعوهم واختاروهم للشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes the verse a reply to Jews who said they would believe if someone other than Gabriel brought revelation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو جواب لليهود، إذ قالوا: لو كان الرسول إلى محمد غير جبريل

rows.speaker: الزجاج وعلي بن سليمان والنحاس
rows.claim: These grammarians treat the pause after ويختار as complete and ما as negative: humans have no choice, which belongs to God.
rows.anchor: ونص الزجاج، وعلي بن سليمان، والنحاس: على أن الوقف على قوله: ويختار تام

rows.speaker: الطبري وابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Tabari and Ibn Abbas take ما as a relative object: God chooses messengers and laws best for people; al-Tabari rejects the negative reading as unsupported by context.
rows.anchor: وذهب الطبري إلى أن ما موصولة منصوبة بيختار، أي ويختار من الرسل والشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative reading faces an objection about a referent preceding its pronoun; the response supplies omitted فيه, as al-Zamakhshari does for a Quranic phrase and a verse by Antara.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن التقدير: ما كان لهم فيه الخيرة، وحذف لدلالة المعنى
